claims.author: andrewtoth
claims.question: why storage write errors should be handled rather than immediately terminating the process
claims.quote: Can you expand on why this is a problem? If there is a storage error, don't we have to crash anyways?

status_by.quote: Handling the exception lets the node report the storage error and run its normal shutdown cleanup.

claims.status_note: author explained that handling the exception allows reporting the error and clean shutdown rather than std::terminate

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: It would be good to find a code pattern that avoids this class of problem wholesale. It doesn't seem a great use of human (or LLM) review time to spend on such issues one-by-one.
claims.request: find a code pattern or compiler/linter check to avoid exception-during-destruction issues wholesale rather than addressing them piecemeal

claims.author: sedited
claims.quote: I would prefer if we'd catch on std::runtime_error. For other exceptions, e.g. allocation failures, it might genuinely be better to immediately terminate.
claims.request: catch std::runtime_error rather than broader exceptions so other failures like allocation errors still terminate immediately
claims.status_note: author updated handlers to catch std::runtime_error and reviewer approved
